question: Did any BASS-II or FLEX test reach the lunar habitat oxygen level (30% or more)?
claim: None of the 129 BASS-II solid-fuel tests reached 30% oxygen (maximum 22.2%); FLEX droplet tests reached up to 34%.
summary_student: Solid materials like plastics and fabrics were never burned in space at the oxygen level planned for a Moon base. Only liquid fuel droplets were tested that high.
summary_professional: BASS-II initial O2: 13.6–22.2% vol (n = 129). FLEX initial O2: 12–34% mole fraction (n = 274). No solid-fuel test in these two investigations at ≥30% O2.

method.formula: For each investigation, take the initial O2 of every test and report the minimum and maximum, compared with the threshold.

columns: O initial ambient composition; mole fraction

assumptions: Uses the initial O2 of each test.
Mole fraction and volume fraction are treated as equal (ideal gas).
limitations: Covers only BASS-II and FLEX, not every solid-fuel investigation in PSI.
No test at 30% means no data, not that these materials are safe or unsafe at 30%.
Oxygen is compared alone; the lunar habitat also has lower pressure, which was not compared here.
warnings: PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data. Lunar conclusions are bounded by microgravity and Earth-gravity results only.

chart.idea: Range bars of the O2 levels tested by BASS-II and FLEX, with a dashed line at the 30% lunar target.
